name: PIŞTI
description: Pişti (pronounced 'Pish-tee') is one of the most beloved card games in Turkey. It is a fishing game where players capture cards from a central pile by matching ranks or playing a Jack (which captures any pile). The name means 'cooked' and refers to the pişti bonus: capturing a single card with a matching rank scores 10 extra points. Fast-paced, with observation and memory.

content.text: Pişti (pronounced 'Pish-tee') is one of the most beloved card games in Turkey. It is a fishing game where players capture cards from a central pile by matching ranks or playing a Jack (which captures any pile). The name means 'cooked' and refers to the pişti bonus: capturing a single card with a matching rank scores 10 extra points. Fast-paced, with observation and memory.
Derived from ancient Central Asian card games and formalized in Turkey during the Ottoman era. It shares roots with the Spanish game 'Escoba'.
2 players (this variant). Also commonly 4 in partnerships or 4 individuals; rules are the same.

Standard 52-card pack (French suits, no jokers). Pişti uses the full deck: four cards are dealt face down to the centre, four to each player, and the remainder forms the stock; one centre card is turned face up to start the pile.

Standard 52-card pack (French suits, no jokers). Pişti uses the full deck: four cards are dealt face down to the centre, four to each player, and the remainder forms the stock; one centre card is turned face up to start the pile.

Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's left cuts. Dealer deals 4 cards face down to the center, then 4 to each player. Remaining cards form the stock. One of the four center cards is turned face up to start the pile (if it is a Jack, turn until a non-Jack). Player to dealer's right plays first. After all play their 4 cards, dealer deals 4 more to each from stock; repeat until stock is exhausted.

items.text: Four in partnerships: Four players in two partnerships, partners sitting opposite. Rules same; play anticlockwise. First team to 151 wins.
Four individuals: Four players each keeping individual score. Same rules; first to 151 wins.

Bluffing variation: When one card is on the table, next player may play a card face down claiming a pişti. If the first player believes it, 10 points; if not and it was a bluff, first player scores 20; if not and it matched, double pişti 20 to the captor.
